hunks.baseline: There are no secrets in the world that can stay secret forever.
hunks.sol: There’s no such thing as a perfect secret.

hunks.baseline: Birds hear what’s said by day, rats hear what’s said by night, and in the end, every word slips from someone’s lips.
hunks.sol: Birds hear what’s said by day, rats hear what’s said by night, and sooner or later, it all comes out of someone’s mouth.

hunks.baseline: At the declaration of the one who’d first let my secret slip—as if a newborn were crying for the first time—the “one person” in question licked his lips.
hunks.sol: The culprit who’d first let my secret slip made his declaration like a newborn letting out its first cry. At that, the “one person” in question licked his lips.

hunks.baseline: “So, I was just planning to check a few facts. It’s not like I could believe a word that crazy old man said.”
hunks.sol: “Well, I was only going to check a few facts. How was I supposed to believe a word that crazy old man said?”

hunks.baseline: I asked in a subdued voice, “And then?”
hunks.sol: “And then?” I asked quietly.

hunks.baseline: “I had no choice. I grabbed the person who seemed to know you best and asked him.”
hunks.sol: “I had no choice but to corner the person who seemed to know you best and ask him.”

hunks.baseline: At the Slaughter Saint’s casually shifted gaze, Hyuk Mujin, who’d been huddled in a corner of the carriage, warily watching the others, stammered out an answer.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint’s gaze shifted to Hyuk Mujin. Huddled in a corner of the carriage, Mujin had been watching everyone’s reactions. Now he stammered out an answer.

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. But he turned out to be surprisingly tight-lipped. He insisted he’d rather die than tell me anything that might put you in danger.”
hunks.sol: “That’s true. But he turned out to be surprisingly tight-lipped. Said he’d rather die than tell me anything that might put you in danger.”

hunks.baseline: “You heard him, right? I’m that loyal.”
hunks.sol: “You heard him, right? That’s how loyal I am.”

hunks.baseline: “So, I had no choice but to tell him a rough version of what I’d heard. Then the very next day, some random weirdo came asking about you.”
hunks.sol: “So I had no choice but to tell him roughly what I’d heard. Then, the very next day, some random fool came asking me about it.”

hunks.baseline: As if perfectly timed, that “random weirdo” suddenly stuck his face into the conversation.
hunks.sol: Right on cue, that “random fool” poked his head in.

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint glared at Cheongpung with tired eyes, then added, “Anyway, I told exactly one person, too.”
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint gave Cheongpung a tired glare, then added, “Anyway, I only told one person, too.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin drew in his shoulders again and muttered, “Me too.”
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin drew his shoulders in again and muttered, “So did I.”

hunks.baseline: Yeah. I figured.
hunks.sol: Yeah. Of course he had.

hunks.baseline: But if I were Hyuk Mujin, I wouldn’t have spilled a “stupendous secret I couldn’t possibly keep to myself” to Cheongpung.
hunks.sol: But if I were Hyuk Mujin, I wouldn’t have shared a “stupendous secret I couldn’t possibly keep to myself” with Cheongpung.

hunks.baseline: Because it was Cheongpung.
hunks.sol: Because he was Cheongpung.

hunks.baseline: Maybe an innocence-proving contest had started without my noticing. Cheongpung shouted with tremendous enthusiasm, and Jeok Cheongang nodded.
hunks.sol: Had an innocence-proving contest started without my noticing? Cheongpung was making his case with tremendous enthusiasm, and Jeok Cheongang nodded.

hunks.baseline: “He’s not wrong. The problem was that he said it at just about that volume, at a meal where most of us were gathered.”
hunks.sol: “He’s not wrong. The problem is that he said it at about that volume, over a meal with most of us gathered around.”

hunks.baseline: I shook my head, then happened to meet someone’s eyes.
hunks.sol: I shook my head and happened to meet someone’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: Unlike everyone else, she’d been silent the whole time, without a reaction. Ju Hwaran.
hunks.sol: Unlike the others, she’d been silent this whole time, without so much as a reaction. Ju Hwaran.

hunks.baseline: She only stared at me, her gaze pricking my face like a thin needle.
hunks.sol: She just looked at me, her gaze pricking my face like a thin needle.

hunks.baseline: A hush had fallen over the carriage, and everyone was watching me.
hunks.sol: A hush had fallen over the carriage. Everyone was watching.

hunks.baseline: Well. I didn’t know.
hunks.sol: Well. I had no idea what to do.

hunks.baseline: I felt like I should say something, but what was I supposed to say? And how?
hunks.sol: I felt like I should say something, but what? And how?

hunks.baseline: My thoughts began tangling like a ball of yarn.
hunks.sol: My thoughts were tangling like a ball of yarn when her tightly closed red lips parted.

hunks.baseline: Then her tightly closed red lips parted.
“Huh? What do you mean, all of a sudden?”
hunks.sol: “Huh? What do you mean?”

hunks.baseline: “I mean, you’re not actually an immortal or something instead of a human, are you?”
hunks.sol: “You’re not actually an immortal or something instead of a human, are you?”

hunks.baseline: I blinked at her blankly. Then, once I understood, I let out a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: I blinked at her. Then I understood and let out a small, disbelieving laugh.

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, an immortal? Do I look that impressive to you?”
hunks.sol: “Come on. Do I look that impressive to you, Young Lady Ju?”

hunks.baseline: “…Oh. Sorry. I didn’t mean to. But really, I’m not.”
hunks.sol: “…Sorry. I couldn’t help it. But I’m really not.”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. What else would I be if not human? Somehow, a misunderstanding piled on top of another, and I got called someone from the realm of immortals. But my hometown is just another place where people live, same as here.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. What else would I be if not human? A few misunderstandings piled up, and somehow my home came to be called the realm of immortals. But people live there just like they do here.”

hunks.baseline: “Is that so?”
hunks.sol: “Really?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah.”
hunks.sol: “Yes.”

hunks.baseline: Calling them the same world would be a huge stretch.
hunks.sol: Calling the two worlds the same would be a huge stretch.

hunks.baseline: Even setting aside the difference in technological development, you wouldn’t run into a monster on your way to the inn at the intersection by your house in this part of the world.
hunks.sol: Even setting aside the difference in technology, at least around here you wouldn’t run into a monster on your way to the inn at the intersection near your house.

hunks.baseline: “…Wait, what?”
hunks.sol: “…Where did that come from?”

hunks.baseline: “I’m just curious. You said only your soul goes back and forth, and that the other world is different from this one.”
hunks.sol: “I’m just curious. You said only your soul goes back and forth, and your world is different from this one.”

hunks.baseline: I answered, sounding a little bewildered.
hunks.sol: I answered, still a little bewildered.

hunks.baseline: “No, I mean, that’s right. After going back and forth a few times, I got a little confused about time for a second…”
hunks.sol: “No, that’s right. Going back and forth a few times has messed up my sense of time, so I got confused for a second…”

hunks.baseline: I’d started rambling out excuses without meaning to when Ju Hwaran cut me off in a voice as sharp as a blade.
hunks.sol: I was starting to ramble out excuses without meaning to when Ju Hwaran cut me off sharply.

hunks.baseline: “And you’re not an immortal or a celestial who’s lived for five hundred years since ascending to immortality.”
hunks.sol: “And you’re not some immortal who ascended five hundred years ago.”

hunks.baseline: Ascending to immortality? Please.
hunks.sol: Ascended to immortality? Please.

hunks.baseline: And if I really were a five-hundred-year-old immortal, the one pulling this eight-horse carriage would be Cheonju, not a horse.
hunks.sol: And if I really were a five-hundred-year-old immortal, the one pulling this eight-horse carriage right now would be the Lord of Heaven, not a horse.

hunks.baseline: I was lost in a thought both sweet and sad when Ju Hwaran delivered her verdict like a judge who’d finished hearing the case.
hunks.sol: I was lost in that sweet, sad thought when Ju Hwaran delivered her verdict like a judge who’d finished hearing the case.

hunks.baseline: No explanation of what the case was about. No sentence.
hunks.sol: No account of the case. No sentence.

hunks.baseline: *No, actually, I think I do know.*
hunks.sol: *No, honestly, I think I do know.*

hunks.baseline: For some reason, my chest felt tight. Somewhere close to my heart.
hunks.sol: For some reason, my chest felt tight. The part near my heart.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, another part of my chest grew heavy.
hunks.sol: At the same time, another part of it grew heavy.

hunks.baseline: I wondered if it was okay to feel this way right now. If I had any right to.
hunks.sol: Was it okay to feel this way right now? Did I have any right to?

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why I couldn’t meet her gaze easily as she kept looking steadily at me through the strange atmosphere, made even stranger by everyone else’s eyes on us.
hunks.sol: Maybe that was why I found it hard to meet her eyes as she kept looking steadily at me, with everyone else watching us and making the air between us stranger still.

hunks.baseline: “Anyway, when will everyone else be back?”
hunks.sol: “Anyway, when will the others be back?”

hunks.baseline: “Hm? What?”
hunks.sol: “H-hm?”

hunks.baseline: “Ahem. Why are you asking that all of a sudden?”
hunks.sol: “Ahem. Why do you ask all of a sudden?”

hunks.baseline: “I missed them. And now that it’s come to this, there’s something I want to tell everyone myself.”
hunks.sol: “I want to see them. And now that it’s come to this, there’s something I’d like to tell everyone myself.”

hunks.baseline: “What? But earlier, that human Cheongpung clearly—”
hunks.sol: “What? But earlier, Cheongpung clearly—”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, he said it all loud enough for everyone to hear. At a meal where *most* of us were gathered.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, that careless mouth of his said it loud enough for everyone to hear. At a meal where *most* of us were gathered.”

hunks.baseline: I let out a short gasp.
hunks.sol: I let out a short exclamation.

hunks.baseline: The Supreme Peak master who’d first crossed paths with us in Gansu and accompanied us all the way here.
hunks.sol: The Supreme Peak master we’d first met in Gansu, who’d accompanied us all the way here.

hunks.baseline: A mysterious eccentric, as puzzling as his wild, unkempt hair—even he didn’t know who he was.
hunks.sol: A mysterious eccentric as baffling as his wild, unkempt hair. Even he didn’t know who he was.

hunks.baseline: “What Great Sir? The guy can lose his mind several times a day.”
hunks.sol: “What Great Sir? The fellow loses his mind several times a day.”

hunks.baseline: “He happened to be there, we couldn’t have helped it. But it still didn’t sit right with this old man to tell him that sort of thing, so I told everyone to keep quiet. He’s been useful enough, but a secret is a secret, and we don’t even know who he is.”
hunks.sol: “If he’d happened to be there, we couldn’t have helped it. But it still didn’t sit right with this old man to go out of my way to tell him, so I told everyone to keep quiet. He’s been quite useful, but a secret is a secret, and we don’t even know who he is.”

hunks.baseline: “Right.”
hunks.sol: “Hmm.”

hunks.baseline: “I can guess what you’re thinking. I’m not about to force my decision on you. So do as you like about that fellow you call Great Sir. But…”
hunks.sol: “I can guess what you’re thinking. I’m not going to force my judgment on you. Do as you like about that fellow you call Great Sir. But…”

hunks.baseline: “There’s someone else I’m more concerned about than him.”
hunks.sol: “There’s someone else I’m more concerned about.”

hunks.baseline: “The people here have more or less understood and accepted it by now. But the world doesn’t work out so easily. Especially for old folks—it’s hard for them to understand something new.”
hunks.sol: “The ones here have more or less understood and accepted it by now. But things don’t always work out so neatly. Old folks especially have trouble understanding anything new.”

hunks.baseline: I muttered the words to myself and looked out the window.
hunks.sol: I looked out the window.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps because of the clouds drifting across the pitch-black night sky, the stars looked especially dim tonight.
hunks.sol: Perhaps because clouds were passing across the pitch-black sky, the stars looked especially dim tonight.

hunks.baseline: By day, the heat seemed ready to burn the whole world. But once the sun set and darkness arrived, an icy chill blanketed the land.
hunks.sol: By day, the heat seemed ready to burn the whole world. Once the sun set and darkness fell, an icy chill blanketed the land.

hunks.baseline: Even through the cold that seeped into her bones, though, the faint shadow standing alone atop a sand dune didn’t waver in the slightest.
hunks.sol: Yet even in the cold that seeped to the bone, the slender shadow cast alone atop a sand dune did not waver.

hunks.baseline: It was only natural. The master who cast the shadow had long since surpassed the realm of Unaffected by Cold and Heat.
hunks.sol: That was only natural. The master who cast it had long since surpassed the realm of Unaffected by Cold and Heat.

hunks.baseline: Bow Saint gazed into the dark desert, her eyes clouded with thought.
hunks.sol: The Bow Saint gazed into the dark desert, her eyes grave.

hunks.baseline: The boundless sea of sand stretched endlessly before her, as if it resembled her heart.
hunks.sol: The boundless sea of sand before her seemed to mirror her heart.

hunks.baseline: As though no matter how far she walked, she’d never see its end—and as though it contained nothing but hardship and gritty grains of sand.
hunks.sol: No end in sight, no matter how far she walked. Nothing within it but hardship and rough grains of sand.

hunks.baseline: Bow Saint murmured in a low voice.
hunks.sol: She murmured the words softly.

hunks.baseline: It never asked anything in return. It simply let the wind pass in silence, the wind no one knew where it had come from.
hunks.sol: It asked no questions. It only let the wind pass through in silence, from wherever that wind had come.

hunks.baseline: But it wasn’t good company.
hunks.sol: But it was no good for conversation.

hunks.baseline: No, even if the desert could speak, that wouldn’t change.
hunks.sol: Even if the desert could speak, that would not change.

hunks.baseline: The person Bow Saint wanted to talk to was someone else.
hunks.sol: The person the Bow Saint wanted to speak to was someone else.

hunks.baseline: Her fingers, as hard as steel and marked with calluses despite her translucent skin, searched inside her robe.
hunks.sol: Her fingers, hard as steel and callused despite her translucent skin, searched inside her robe.

hunks.baseline: The old letter the Martial God had left only for her—and which, for that reason, she couldn’t tell anyone about—was caught between the folds of her clothes.
hunks.sol: Through the fabric, they found the old letter the Martial God had left for her alone, containing a secret she therefore could tell no one.

hunks.baseline: Bow Saint couldn’t understand.
hunks.sol: The Bow Saint could not understand.

hunks.baseline: She had believed and followed what the letter said only because the Martial God had left it. From the beginning until now, she had never been able to make sense of its contents.
hunks.sol: She had trusted and followed the letter’s instructions only because the Martial God had left it. From the beginning until now, she had never been able to make sense of what it said.

hunks.baseline: And after hearing Jin Taekyung’s secret just a few days ago, she found it even harder to understand.
hunks.sol: And since hearing Jin Taekyung’s secret a few days ago, she understood it even less.

hunks.baseline: A faint sound from behind reached Bow Saint’s ears.
hunks.sol: A faint sound behind her reached the Bow Saint’s ears.
